z-m-03-01.title: Long thin paper and plump paper: which one get bigger area?
z-m-03-01.topic: Compare area (put one on top the other, and compare with squares wey get the same size)
z-m-03-01.goal: Compare area of two papers wey shape look different by eye, overlaying dem, and comparing with same-size squares; adjust your judgment as you go. If overlay no settle am, talk say another method dey needed.
z-m-03-01.material: Two rectangular papers, '가' and '나', made from thick paper. '가' wide and long; '나' shorter and plumper. You wan find which one get bigger area (size of surface paper cover). You never measure lengths yet.
z-m-03-01.thinking.1: Changing your confidence as new information come
z-m-03-01.prereq.0: Knowing 'wide/narrow' and comparing two things by putting one over other (Grade 1 level)
z-m-03-01.s.s1.prompt: Information go show piece by piece. Each time, choose which one you think get bigger area.
z-m-03-01.s.s1.hint.0: At each stage, talk one thing about 'wetin same and wetin different' in new information.
z-m-03-01.s.s1.hint.1: Imagine cut both papers and put one on top the other, then use finger trace parts wey stick out.
z-m-03-01.s.s1.st.0.info: Both papers dey apart for desk and you only look. '가' look long and '나' look plump.
z-m-03-01.s.s1.st.0.ask: Right now, which one you think get bigger area?
z-m-03-01.s.s1.st.0.after: E hard to decide only by how e look. You need method like putting dem together or compare with same-size pieces.
z-m-03-01.s.s1.st.0.o.a: 가 bigger. E wider, so long one bigger.
z-m-03-01.s.s1.st.0.r.a: You look only at length in one direction. For area, you must consider width and height together.
z-m-03-01.s.s1.st.0.o.b: You no fit tell by looking alone. You must put dem over each other or measure.
z-m-03-01.s.s1.st.0.r.b: You first think of way to check. Na good habit to separate feeling from checking.
z-m-03-01.s.s1.st.0.o.c: 나 bigger. E plump, so e look fuller.
z-m-03-01.s.s1.st.0.r.c: You decide by feeling. E fit be right, but you no fit know before checking.
z-m-03-01.s.s1.st.0.o.d: The shapes different, so of course areas different. We just no know which bigger.
z-m-03-01.s.s1.st.0.r.d: Even when shapes different, areas fit equal. We no get reason yet to state am so firmly.
z-m-03-01.s.s1.st.1.info: You put '가' on top of '나' and match upper-left corners. '가' stick out to right, and '나' stick out below '가'. Neither cover the other completely.
z-m-03-01.s.s1.st.1.after: If one cover the other fully, covered one get smaller area. But if both stick out, overlay alone no make decision easy.
z-m-03-01.s.s1.st.1.o.a: 가 bigger. The part wey stick out continue far to right.
z-m-03-01.s.s1.st.1.r.a: You only look at length of part wey stick out. Think also about how 나 stick out below.
z-m-03-01.s.s1.st.1.o.b: 나 bigger. The part wey stick out below look thicker.
z-m-03-01.s.s1.st.1.r.b: E fit look like that, but you never compare how big both sticking-out parts be.
z-m-03-01.s.s1.st.1.o.c: Both areas same. Parts wey stick out look almost alike.
z-m-03-01.s.s1.st.1.r.c: Looking alike no reason to say dem same. Dem fit be, but you need check more.
z-m-03-01.s.s1.st.1.o.d: Overlaying alone no decide am. Another method needed too.
z-m-03-01.s.s1.st.1.r.d: You notice say when both stick out after overlay, you no fit tell quickly which bigger.
z-m-03-01.s.s1.st.2.info: Both papers get same-size small square cells, with no gaps. '가' get 2 rows of 6 cells across; '나' get 3 rows of 4 cells across.
z-m-03-01.s.s1.st.2.ask: If you compare by cells, which one get bigger area?
z-m-03-01.s.s1.st.2.after: 가 get 2 rows of 6 cells, 나 3 rows of 4, and cells same size, so both get 12 cells. So although shapes different, areas same. If cells sizes different, this method no work.
z-m-03-01.s.s1.st.2.o.a: Both papers get 12 cells, same number, so areas same.
z-m-03-01.s.s1.st.2.r.a: You compare by total cell count because cells same size. You think about shape and area separately.
z-m-03-01.s.s1.st.2.o.b: 가 bigger. One row get 6 cells, more than 4.
z-m-03-01.s.s1.st.2.r.b: You look only at one row. You must also consider how many rows dey.
z-m-03-01.s.s1.st.2.o.c: 나 bigger. E get 3 rows, more than 2.
z-m-03-01.s.s1.st.2.r.c: You look only at row count. You must also consider cells per row.
z-m-03-01.s.s1.st.2.o.d: If shapes different, you no fit compare areas by counting cells.
z-m-03-01.s.s1.st.2.r.d: If cells same size, you fit compare total number even if shapes different.
z-m-03-01.s.s1.reflect: How your thinking change from first looking, to overlaying, to comparing cells? For cell comparison, wetin must be same about cells?
z-m-03-01.s.s2.prompt: One friend talk, 'Shapes different, so areas different too!' Wetin you wan tell your friend?
z-m-03-01.s.s2.hint.0: Look for example among papers wey you just see wey show your friend's statement wrong.
z-m-03-01.s.s2.hint.1: First write which numbers you fit use as evidence in that example, then make sentence.
z-m-03-01.s.s2.selfAssess.0: The evidence numbers you write (like cell count) really belong to these papers?
z-m-03-01.s.s2.selfAssess.1: You talk separately say 'shapes different' and 'areas different'?
z-m-03-01.s.s2.selfAssess.2: You also mention condition say cells same size?
z-m-03-01.s.s2.model.0: Both get 12 cells, so areas same. Even if shapes different, areas fit same.
z-m-03-01.s.s2.model.1: I no fit tell by overlaying, but when I count same-size cells, both 가 and 나 get 12. So areas same.

z-m-03-06.prereq.0: Count and Add Numbers up to 10
z-m-03-06.title: As I look down from above, I see 3, so how many hide below?
z-m-03-06.topic: Shapes wey stack (think about the parts wey you no fit see)
z-m-03-06.goal: Separate wetin you fit talk for sure and wetin you no fit talk from only the view from above, then make different ways to stack them wey look the same from above and get the same total number of blocks.
z-m-03-06.material: Dem build three towers side by side with blocks of the same size. One dey left, one for middle and one dey right. Each tower stack from floor, and each get between 1 and 3 layers. If you look down from above, na only the top block of each tower you see. You no fit see from above how many block layers dey below.
z-m-03-06.thinking.0: Separate wetin you know for sure from wetin you no know based on wetin you see
z-m-03-06.thinking.1: Make plenty answers within the conditions
z-m-03-06.thinking.2: Explain why the shape no change
z-m-03-06.prereq.1: Know up, down, left and right
z-m-03-06.s.s1.prompt: Na only the view from above you know. Choose everything wey you fit talk for sure from this alone.
z-m-03-06.s.s1.hint.0: Separate the blocks wey you fit see from the ones wey hide below.
z-m-03-06.s.s1.hint.1: Test one by one whether each statement always true even if the towers get different number of layers.
z-m-03-06.s.s1.r.a: You count only the top blocks wey you fit see. Think whether more blocks fit dey on the lower layers.
z-m-03-06.s.s1.r.b: Na fact wey you fit know for sure from the view from above. Look again whether you miss anything.
z-m-03-06.s.s1.r.d: Na fact wey you fit know for sure from the view from above. Look again whether you miss anything.
z-m-03-06.s.s1.r.c: You decide from the beginning say every tower get 2 layers. Anybody talk so?
z-m-03-06.s.s1.r.e: 3 layers na only the tallest one wey fit be, and from above you no fit see which tower get 3 layers.
z-m-03-06.s.s1.explain: From above, na only the 3 top blocks you see, so the only things you know for sure be say 3 towers dey and at least 3 blocks dey. The lower layers fit be 1 to 3, so total dey between 3 and 9, and you no fit talk the exact number.
z-m-03-06.s.s2.prompt: Make 3 different ways to choose the layer numbers for the three towers so total go be 7 blocks. The view from above must remain the same.
z-m-03-06.s.s2.hint.0: First find one case where the layer numbers of the three towers add up to 7.
z-m-03-06.s.s2.hint.1: Each tower get between 1 and 3 layers. Make another way by removing one layer from one tower and adding one layer to another.
z-m-03-06.s.s2.var.p: Number of layers for the left tower
z-m-03-06.s.s2.var.q: Number of layers for the middle tower
z-m-03-06.s.s2.var.r: Number of layers for the right tower
z-m-03-06.s.s2.ok.c0: The layer numbers na natural numbers.
z-m-03-06.s.s2.fail.c0: The layer number must be counting number like 1, 2, 3.
z-m-03-06.s.s2.ok.c1: All three towers get between 1 and 3 layers.
z-m-03-06.s.s2.fail.c1: Towers get between 1 and 3 layers. With 0 layers, nobody go see am from above, and you no fit make 4 or more layers.
z-m-03-06.s.s2.fail.c2: The layer numbers for the three towers must add up to 7 blocks.
z-m-03-06.s.s2.explain: The cases wey the layer numbers add up to 7 na (1, 3, 3), (3, 1, 3), (3, 3, 1), (2, 2, 3), (2, 3, 2), (3, 2, 2), na six ways. For every one, na only the 3 top blocks you see from above, so the view look exactly the same.
z-m-03-06.s.s2.because.prompt: Choose one way wey you make and explain why the view from above remain the same.
z-m-03-06.s.s2.because.hint.0: Talk which blocks you fit see and which ones hide when you look down from above.
z-m-03-06.s.s2.because.hint.1: Check whether changing the number of layers for one tower change the number of blocks wey you see from above.
z-m-03-06.s.s2.because.selfAssess.0: For the way wey I choose, all three spaces for the back row dey level with or below the front row?
z-m-03-06.s.s2.because.selfAssess.1: You give the reason 'dem hide, so you no fit see them'?
z-m-03-06.s.s2.because.model.0: If you look down from above, na only the 3 top blocks you see, and the blocks below hide under the ones above. So even if the layer numbers different, the view look the same.
z-m-03-06.s.s2.because.model.1: I stack 3 layers, 3 layers and 1 layer. From above you see only one top block for each tower, and the lower layers hide, so you no fit see them.
z-m-03-06.s.s2.because.model.2: From above, the blocks below hide inside the tower and you no fit see them. So the shape wey you see remain the same.

z-m-03-02.title: A string hang between two nails on wall: length same too?
z-m-03-02.topic: Comparing length (straight route and bent route)
z-m-03-02.goal: Find wrong line for idea say two strings with same start and end must have same length. Say wetin else dem need before claiming lengths same, and how to check.
z-m-03-02.material: Two nails dey for wall. Jia hang one string wey no stretch tight between nails. Minho hang another unstretched string on same nails but make am sag. Both strings start at left nail and end at right nail. Jia reason like this.
z-m-03-02.thinking.2: Saying how to check and expected result
z-m-03-02.prereq.0: Knowing 'long/short' and comparing straight things by putting ends together (Grade 1 level)
z-m-03-02.s.s1.prompt: Choose first line in Jia thinking wey wrong.
z-m-03-02.s.s1.hint.0: Sort each line into fact you check with eyes or idea wey come from facts.
z-m-03-02.s.s1.hint.1: Draw and compare shape of string pulled tight with one wey sag.
z-m-03-02.s.s1.line.0: My string tight, Minho own sag down.
z-m-03-02.s.s1.line.1: Still, both strings hang on left nail and right nail.
z-m-03-02.s.s1.line.2: Start and end same places, so two strings same length too.
z-m-03-02.s.s1.line.3: So even if we pull Minho string tight, e go same length as my string.
z-m-03-02.s.s1.explain: Line 3 first wrong. Even if start and end same, length fit differ depending whether route straight or curved. Line 4 conclusion follow line 3 thinking, so na mistake afterward. Lines 1 and 2 tell wetin dem see as e be.
z-m-03-02.s.s2.prompt: Minho string no stretch too, like Jia own. Right now only Minho string dey sag. Wetin other condition we need before we fit say both strings get same length?
z-m-03-02.s.s2.hint.0: Talk wetin different about how dem hang both strings.
z-m-03-02.s.s2.hint.1: Check one by one whether string length fit change if each condition change.
z-m-03-02.s.s2.r.a: Color no concern length. Look for things connected to length.
z-m-03-02.s.s2.o.b: Both strings start at left nail and end at right nail
z-m-03-02.s.s2.r.b: Dem already tell us that. As you see before, same start and end no set length.
z-m-03-02.s.s2.o.c: Both strings hang straight and taut
z-m-03-02.s.s2.o.d: Both nails dey same height on wall
z-m-03-02.s.s2.r.d: Whether nails same height no matter; both strings hung on same two places. How string hang matter more.
z-m-03-02.s.s2.explain: When both strings hang on same nails and both tight, both follow straightest path, so length same. If one sags, that string fit be longer.
z-m-03-02.s.s3.prompt: You wan find whether Minho string same length as Jia own. Write how to check and what result you expect.
z-m-03-02.s.s3.hint.0: Imagine untying both strings from nails and laying dem on desk.
z-m-03-02.s.s3.hint.1: Imagine wetin happen to other ends when you line up one end of each string.
z-m-03-02.s.s3.selfAssess.0: The method I describe really show difference in both strings' length?
z-m-03-02.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You connect reason for expected result to 'sagging/tight'?
z-m-03-02.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You think whether both strings still fit turn out same length?
z-m-03-02.s.s3.model.0: Pull Minho string tight and put beside Jia string. I think sagging string go longer.
z-m-03-02.s.s3.model.1: Straighten both strings, match one end, and see where other end land; you go know lengths fit differ.
z-m-03-02.s.s3.modelNote.1: Expected result short, but e state both method and possibility.

z-m-03-03.title: If you cut square paper once with straight cut, wetin pieces go look like?
z-m-03-03.topic: Dividing flat shapes (pointed corners of pieces from one straight cut)
z-m-03-03.goal: Use number of pointed corners to work out shapes of two pieces you fit make with one straight cut, then find and describe plenty possible cases yourself.
z-m-03-03.material: One square paper get 4 corners. Cut am once with scissors along straight line, dividing into two pieces. Cut join two points on two different edges. Point fit dey at corner or somewhere middle of edge.
z-m-03-03.thinking.0: Finding possible cases by changing where you cut
z-m-03-03.thinking.1: Sorting cases wey no fit conditions
z-m-03-03.thinking.2: Explaining in words how you cut
z-m-03-03.prereq.0: Knowing triangle and quadrilateral shapes and pointing to 'pointed corner' (where two straight lines meet)
z-m-03-03.s.s1.prompt: You cut paper once with straight line and get two pieces. If you add pointed corners on both pieces, how total compare with 4 corners of original paper?
z-m-03-03.s.s1.hint.0: Fold paper small and cut once with scissors, then count corners on each piece.
z-m-03-03.s.s1.hint.1: Add number you count and compare total with 4 corners of original paper.
z-m-03-03.s.s1.o.a: Same as 4. Dem only split paper into two.
z-m-03-03.s.s1.r.a: You only think about corners wey already dey. Wetin happen at two ends of cut line?
z-m-03-03.s.s1.r.b: Paper getting smaller different from corner number. Think about new corners wey form where cut happen.
z-m-03-03.s.s1.o.c: Depending where you cut, e fit be less or more than 4.
z-m-03-03.s.s1.r.c: Separate parts wey change depending on cut place from parts wey always same.
z-m-03-03.s.s1.o.d: More than 4. Corners also form where cut happen.
z-m-03-03.s.s1.r.d: You think about how cut ends make new corners on both pieces.
z-m-03-03.s.s1.explain: When you cut paper, pointed corners show on both pieces at both ends of cut. Count together, total always pass 4 (between 6 and 8).
z-m-03-03.s.s2.prompt: Write corner counts of both pieces from one straight cut as pair (smaller, bigger), and make 3 different pairs. If pieces get same count, write number twice. You fit try by cutting paper.
z-m-03-03.s.s2.hint.0: As you cut paper for real, move both ends of cut line to different places along edges.
z-m-03-03.s.s2.hint.1: Compare how corners of pieces change when one end dey at pointed corner versus middle of edge.
z-m-03-03.s.s2.hint.2: Instead of finding another way to make same pair, look for different pair.
z-m-03-03.s.s2.var.p: Corner count for piece with fewer corners (or that number if equal)
z-m-03-03.s.s2.var.q: Corner count for piece with more corners
z-m-03-03.s.s2.ok.c0: Number of pointed corners na natural number.
z-m-03-03.s.s2.fail.c0: Pointed corner count na counting number like 1, 2, 3.
z-m-03-03.s.s2.ok.c1: p na 3 or more, and no bigger than q.
z-m-03-03.s.s2.fail.c1: Each piece enclosed by straight lines, so e get 3 or more corners; write smaller count first.
z-m-03-03.s.s2.ok.c2: Sum of pointed corners for both pieces na 8 or less.
z-m-03-03.s.s2.fail.c2: With one straight cut, you no fit make corner counts add up pass 8.
z-m-03-03.s.s2.explain: Possible pairs na (3, 3), (3, 4), (3, 5), (4, 4). Join two opposite corners to get (3, 3). Join one corner to middle of opposite edge to get (3, 4). Join middle parts of two neighboring edges and cut off one corner to get (3, 5). Join middle parts of two opposite edges to get (4, 4). You no fit make pair with 2 corners or sum 9 or more.
z-m-03-03.s.s2.because.prompt: Choose one pair you make and describe in words how you cut paper.
z-m-03-03.s.s2.because.hint.0: First say whether each end of cut line dey at pointed corner or middle of edge.
z-m-03-03.s.s2.because.hint.1: Name shapes of both pieces (triangle, quadrilateral, etc.).
z-m-03-03.s.s2.because.selfAssess.0: With cut method I describe, na that (p, q) go really come out?
z-m-03-03.s.s2.because.selfAssess.1: E clear where you put both ends?
z-m-03-03.s.s2.because.model.0: If you cut along line joining two opposite pointed corners, you get 2 triangle pieces; each get 3 pointed corners.
z-m-03-03.s.s2.because.model.1: If you join middle parts of two neighboring edges and cut off one corner, small triangle piece get 3 pointed corners and big piece get 5.

z-m-03-04.title: Which box heart and star cookies suppose enter?
z-m-03-04.topic: Sorting flat shapes (triangles, quadrilaterals, circles, and shapes wey no be any of these)
z-m-03-04.goal: When shape no fit sort into three boxes, choose sorting standard again, make your own sorting rule, and explain with reasons.
z-m-03-04.material: Cookie shop wan put flat cookies into boxes based on shape. Three boxes: 'triangle box', 'quadrilateral box', and 'circle box'. Cookies: 2 triangle shapes, 3 square shapes, 4 circle shapes, 2 heart shapes, 1 star shape. Star get 5 pointed corners and all edges straight. Heart top edge get curved line and one pointed corner below.
z-m-03-04.thinking.0: Checking whether sorting standard cover all cases
z-m-03-04.thinking.1: Changing standard or making new one
z-m-03-04.thinking.2: Knowing many different rules fit be possible
z-m-03-04.prereq.0: Know triangle, quadrilateral and circle shapes (Grade 1 level)
z-m-03-04.prereq.1: Tell straight lines and curved lines apart
z-m-03-04.s.s1.prompt: Which box go fit the star biscuit?

z-m-03-04.s.s1.hint.1: Compare biscuit for triangle box with the star, then talk one thing wey be the same and one wey different.
z-m-03-04.s.s1.o.a: Make new box. E no fit any of the three boxes.
z-m-03-04.s.s1.r.a: You notice say with the rule wey dey now, no place dey to put am.
z-m-03-04.s.s1.o.b: The circle box. E small and flat, so e look like circle.
z-m-03-04.s.s1.r.b: Size and flatness no be rule to sort shapes. Look at the edges.
z-m-03-04.s.s1.o.c: The triangle box. E get pointed corners, so e look like triangle.
z-m-03-04.s.s1.r.c: You only look at the pointed corners. The star get 5 pointed corners, so e different from triangle.
z-m-03-04.s.s1.o.d: The quadrilateral box. E get plenty pointed corners, so e near quadrilateral.
z-m-03-04.s.s1.r.d: You only look at the plenty pointed corners. Quadrilateral get 4 straight lines.
z-m-03-04.s.s1.explain: Star na shape wey 5 straight lines surround, so e no be triangle, quadrilateral, or circle. You need make new box or change the rule.
z-m-03-04.s.s1.acc.0: If you make the rule wider and rename the boxes, like 'shapes wey get pointed corners', you fit put them like this too. Then you need change the name 'triangle box'.
z-m-03-04.s.s2.prompt: Choose everything wey good sorting rule suppose get.
z-m-03-04.s.s2.hint.0: Try put the star and heart under the first rule, then check whether box dey for them.
z-m-03-04.s.s2.hint.1: Imagine say you and your friend each put the same biscuits inside boxes, and check whether dem go the same box.
z-m-03-04.s.s2.o.a: The box names short, so e easy to write and talk
z-m-03-04.s.s2.r.a: Names wey easy to write dey convenient, but e different from whether the rule sort well.
z-m-03-04.s.s2.o.b: Any biscuit wey show up, at least one box dey for am
z-m-03-04.s.s2.r.b: You think say e must fit put every biscuit somewhere without leaving any out.
z-m-03-04.s.s2.o.c: The same biscuit go the same box no matter who dey do am

z-m-03-04.s.s3.prompt: Choose sorting rule wey fit all the biscuits, including heart and star. Write how you divide the boxes and which box heart and star go.
z-m-03-04.s.s3.hint.0: Instead of the current box names 'triangle, quadrilateral, circle', try sort by the biscuit edge features (straight lines, curved lines).
z-m-03-04.s.s3.hint.1: Put the 12 biscuits one by one under your rule and check say no biscuit remain out or enter two places.
z-m-03-04.s.s3.placeholder: Example: The heart and the star ...

z-m-03-04.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You talk with reasons where heart and star go?

z-m-03-05.title: The teddy bear wey dey my right dey which side of my friend?
z-m-03-05.topic: Position and direction (left and right dey change according to the direction wey person face)
z-m-03-05.goal: Explain when my left and right and my friend's left and right be the same, and when dem opposite, using the direction wey person face as condition.
z-m-03-05.material: Teddy bear dey on desk. I sit for one side of desk, and teddy bear dey my right side. One friend dey near the desk, but e never talk where e dey or which way e face.
z-m-03-05.thinking.0: Find the conditions wey you need to judge
z-m-03-05.thinking.1: Imagine how e look from another seat
z-m-03-05.thinking.2: Explain conclusion wey dey change according to conditions
z-m-03-05.prereq.0: Know left and right and point directions with your own body (Grade 1 level)
z-m-03-05.prereq.1: Know front, back, and facing one another
z-m-03-05.s.s1.prompt: The teddy bear dey which side of my friend?
z-m-03-05.s.s1.hint.0: Put pencil on desk like the teddy bear, and as you sit down, point your right hand to the pencil.
z-m-03-05.s.s1.hint.1: Imagine separately the case where your friend stand in front of you and the case where dem stand behind you.
z-m-03-05.s.s1.o.a: E dey my friend's left. My friend must dey sit for the side opposite me.
z-m-03-05.s.s1.r.a: You assume from the beginning say your friend dey sit opposite you and face you. Anybody talk that one?
z-m-03-05.s.s1.o.b: We no fit decide. We need know more about where my friend dey and which way my friend face.
z-m-03-05.s.s1.r.b: You notice say dem never give the conditions wey you need to decide.
z-m-03-05.s.s1.o.c: E dey my friend's right. If e dey my right, e go dey my friend's right too.
z-m-03-05.s.s1.r.c: You assume say your friend face the same way as me. You check which way your friend face?
z-m-03-05.s.s1.o.d: E dey in front or behind my friend. E dey sit on the desk.
z-m-03-05.s.s1.r.d: You mix front/back with left/right. To say bear dey my right side mean say e dey by the side.
z-m-03-05.s.s1.explain: Left and right dey change depending on whether your friend face the same way as you or face you. If you no know where your friend sit and which way e face, you no fit decide. (E good to first talk your assumption, like 'make we suppose say we face each other' or 'make we suppose say we face the same way', then answer. Make we try that for the next step.)
z-m-03-05.s.s2.prompt: Dem tell you something new: 'My friend dey sit for the opposite side of desk, facing me. The teddy bear still dey my right side.' Which side of my friend the teddy bear dey?
z-m-03-05.s.s2.hint.0: Stand facing your friend and make both of una raise right hands. The two hands dey the same side?
z-m-03-05.s.s2.hint.1: When bear dey my right, find wetin dey my friend's right side.
z-m-03-05.s.s2.r.a: You think say when una face each other, my right side go turn my friend's left side.
z-m-03-05.s.s2.r.b: You move my right straight across to my friend's right. Wetin change when una face each other?
z-m-03-05.s.s2.o.c: Directly in front or behind my friend
z-m-03-05.s.s2.r.c: You mix front/back with the side. The bear dey my right side, that is, by the side.
z-m-03-05.s.s2.explain: When una face each other, each person's left and right opposite. The teddy bear for my right dey my friend's left.
z-m-03-05.s.s3.prompt: This time my friend stand directly behind me, facing the same way as me. Which side of my friend the teddy bear dey? Also talk how this different from when una face each other.
z-m-03-05.s.s3.hint.0: Use your body act am: which side be the right hand of a friend wey stand behind me facing the same way?
z-m-03-05.s.s3.hint.1: Compare whether both people's right hands dey the same side when dem face each other and when dem face the same way.
z-m-03-05.s.s3.placeholder: Example: E dey on the right ...
z-m-03-05.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You talk say my answer na because of the condition 'the direction wey my friend face'?
z-m-03-05.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You compare the case of facing each other with the case of facing the same way?
z-m-03-05.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You think of cases too where you go need answer differently depending on where my friend dey stand?
z-m-03-05.s.s3.model.0: E dey on the right. My friend face the same way as me, so my right and my friend's right dey the same side.
z-m-03-05.s.s3.model.1: I think say e dey my friend's right too. When una face each other, e turn opposite, but when una face the same way, e no turn opposite.
z-m-03-05.s.s3.model.2: E dey my friend's right. If both of us look the same direction, our right hands dey the same side, so e no switch like when we face each other.

z-m-03-07.title: If we only put sticks side by side two at a time, we fit know the lengths of the other two?
z-m-03-07.topic: Compare lengths indirectly (join results from comparing two at a time)
z-m-03-07.goal: Tell apart the cases where joining the results of comparing two at a time let you say the lengths of two sticks wey you no put side by side, from cases where e no let you; make many possible answers for cases wey you no fit decide.
z-m-03-07.material: Red, blue and yellow sticks dey. All straight and no dey stretch. You no fit put all three side by side at once; you fit only put two side by side at a time. We talk the length of a stick as 'number of steps'. For the steps below, dem go tell you wetin happen when dem put two side by side.
z-m-03-07.thinking.0: Reason with information wey you already know
z-m-03-07.thinking.1: Sort out cases where the information no enough
z-m-03-07.thinking.2: Make and show all possible cases
z-m-03-07.prereq.0: Put two sticks side by side and talk which one long pass (Grade 1 level)
z-m-03-07.prereq.1: Talk stick length as 'number of steps'
z-m-03-07.s.s1.prompt: When dem put two side by side, dem talk say 'red long pass blue, and blue long pass yellow'. Dem never put red and yellow side by side. Which one long pass?
z-m-03-07.s.s1.hint.0: Put blue stick for middle and draw the result of comparing red and yellow each with blue.
z-m-03-07.s.s1.hint.1: Make we suppose blue na 5 steps, then write the numbers red and yellow fit each be.
z-m-03-07.s.s1.o.a: Yellow long pass. Dem mention am last, so e long pass.
z-m-03-07.s.s2.o.b: Yellow long pass. Dem mention am last, so e long pass.
z-m-03-07.s.s1.r.a: You mix the order wey dem talk things with the length. Join the two results wey dem tell you.
z-m-03-07.s.s1.o.b: Red long pass. You fit join the comparisons through blue wey dey middle.
z-m-03-07.s.s1.r.b: You join the two comparisons together.
z-m-03-07.s.s1.o.c: The two sticks get the same length, because blue dey between them.
z-m-03-07.s.s1.r.c: Having one stick for middle no make other two equal.
z-m-03-07.s.s1.o.d: You no go know until you put dem side by side yourself.
z-m-03-07.s.s1.r.d: Directly checking sure pass, but sometimes you fit know by linking two results you already get.
z-m-03-07.s.s1.explain: If red longer than blue and blue longer than yellow, red longer than yellow. Middle stick na bridge between dem.
z-m-03-07.s.s2.prompt: This time results different. Dem say 'red longer than blue, and yellow too longer than blue.' Red and yellow never put side by side. Which longer?
z-m-03-07.s.s2.hint.0: Set blue as 5 steps and give red and yellow any numbers from 6 up.
z-m-03-07.s.s2.hint.1: Change numbers for red and yellow and check all cases where each one longer.
z-m-03-07.s.s2.o.a: Red longer. Dem mention its name first, so e longer.
z-m-03-07.s.s2.r.a: You mix order of talking with length. For results dem give, any direct comparison between red and yellow?
z-m-03-07.s.s2.r.b: You mix order of talking with length. For results dem give, any direct comparison between red and yellow?
z-m-03-07.s.s2.o.c: Dem same length because both longer than blue.
z-m-03-07.s.s2.r.c: Both being longer than blue no mean say dem equal. Their lengths fit differ.
z-m-03-07.s.s2.o.d: We no fit decide. Either one fit be longer and both results still correct.
z-m-03-07.s.s2.r.d: You notice say information dem give no settle am.
z-m-03-07.s.s2.explain: If you only know both longer than blue, either red or yellow fit longer, or dem fit same. You need put dem side by side or get other information.
z-m-03-07.s.s3.prompt: Keep result 'red longer than blue and yellow also longer than blue'; make 3 different stick-length sets where which one longer (or whether same) changes. Lengths na natural numbers (step count) from 1 to 30.
z-m-03-07.s.s3.hint.0: First choose length of blue stick. Make red and yellow longer than that.
z-m-03-07.s.s3.hint.1: Make one example where red longer than yellow, then change both numbers to make opposite case.
z-m-03-07.s.s3.hint.2: Include same-length case too. For third example, give red and yellow same number.
z-m-03-07.s.s3.ok.c0: All three lengths na natural numbers from 1 to 30.
z-m-03-07.s.s3.fail.c0: Write lengths as natural numbers (step count) from 1 to 30.
z-m-03-07.s.s3.fail.c1: Red must be longer than blue.
z-m-03-07.s.s3.fail.c2: Yellow also must be longer than blue.
z-m-03-07.s.s3.explain: For example, if (red, blue, yellow) na (10, 5, 8), red longer; if (8, 5, 10), yellow longer; and if (7, 5, 7), dem same. For all three cases, both sticks longer than blue, just as result talk. So this result alone no compare red with yellow.

z-m-03-08.title: If object from above look like circle, wetin kind object fit be?
z-m-03-08.topic: Solid shapes (box, round column, and ball look different depending on viewing direction)
z-m-03-08.goal: Work out whether one view alone fit decide object; narrow your judgment as you learn views from other sides; predict how shape go look when laid sideways.
z-m-03-08.material: One object dey on desk and screen cover am so only part show. E be one of these: box shape (square faces), round-column shape (round and flat top/bottom like tin), or ball shape. E stand upright on floor.
z-m-03-08.thinking.0: Thinking of every possibility from one piece of information
z-m-03-08.thinking.2: Predicting shape when viewing direction change
z-m-03-08.prereq.0: Knowing box, round-column (tin), and ball shapes (Grade 1 level)
z-m-03-08.s.s1.prompt: Viewing directions go increase one by one. Each time, choose what you think object be.
z-m-03-08.s.s1.hint.0: Imagine looking down at each of three objects and talk how each one look.
z-m-03-08.s.s1.hint.1: If you get real can or ball, look from above and side, find wetin same and different.
z-m-03-08.s.s1.st.0.info: Looking down from above, e look like circle.
z-m-03-08.s.s1.st.0.ask: Wetin you think object fit be?
z-m-03-08.s.s1.st.0.after: Box look like square from above, while round column and ball look like circle from above. So with only this information, hard to choose between round column and ball.
z-m-03-08.s.s1.st.0.o.a: Na box shape. Things on desk often be boxes.
z-m-03-08.s.s1.st.0.r.a: You never check how box wey look round from above fit be. How box look from above?
z-m-03-08.s.s1.st.0.o.b: Na ball shape, because e look like circle.
z-m-03-08.s.s1.st.0.r.b: You never check whether circle-look objects na only one. How other objects look?
z-m-03-08.s.s1.st.0.o.c: Na round column or ball. E no look like box.
z-m-03-08.s.s1.st.0.r.c: You consider all cases wey look like circle.
z-m-03-08.s.s1.st.0.o.d: All three fit be possible. Any object look round from above.
z-m-03-08.s.s1.st.0.r.d: Box look square from above. No be all three fit be possible.
z-m-03-08.s.s1.st.1.info: From side, e look square, and top and bottom flat.
z-m-03-08.s.s1.st.1.ask: Now, wetin you think object fit be?
z-m-03-08.s.s1.st.1.after: Object wey look circle from above and square from side na round column. Ball also look circle from side, and box look square from above.
z-m-03-08.s.s1.st.1.o.a: Na round column. From above e look circle, and from side e look square.
z-m-03-08.s.s1.st.1.r.a: You match shapes seen from both directions together.
z-m-03-08.s.s1.st.1.o.b: Na ball. E look circle from above, so e go same from side.
z-m-03-08.s.s1.st.1.r.b: Ball look like circle from any direction. Check whether e fit match side view.
z-m-03-08.s.s1.st.1.o.c: Na box because e look square from side.
z-m-03-08.s.s1.st.1.r.c: You look only at side shape. Also remember say above view was circle.
z-m-03-08.s.s1.st.1.o.d: E circle from above and square from side, so we no fit decide object.
z-m-03-08.s.s1.st.1.r.d: You never work out whether both shapes fit one object. Which object get both shapes?
z-m-03-08.s.s1.st.2.info: This object laid on side and propped up so e no roll.
z-m-03-08.s.s1.st.2.ask: If you look down at object wey dey on side, how e go look?
z-m-03-08.s.s1.st.2.after: When e laid down, side faces up. Square shape wey you see from side when e stand now dey seen from above. Same object fit look different from above depending how e placed.
z-m-03-08.s.s1.st.2.o.a: E look circle. From above e always circle.
z-m-03-08.s.s1.st.2.r.a: You carry over old top view when e was standing. When e laid down, different face point up.
z-m-03-08.s.s1.st.2.o.b: E look like two overlapping circles because e get top and bottom faces.
z-m-03-08.s.s1.st.2.r.b: Even though e get top and bottom faces, when laid down, side dey point up.
z-m-03-08.s.s1.st.2.o.c: E look triangle. When laid down, pointed corners show.
z-m-03-08.s.s1.st.2.r.c: Even if you lay column down, no pointed corners show. Think about shape you saw from side.
z-m-03-08.s.s1.st.2.o.d: E look like long rectangle. When laid down, side face up.
z-m-03-08.s.s1.st.2.r.d: You think side view from before become above view when e laid down.
z-m-03-08.s.s1.reflect: How your thinking change when you knew only above view versus when you also knew side view? To narrow possible objects, what more information needed?
z-m-03-08.s.s2.prompt: Friend talk, 'It look circle from above, so na ball!' Wetin else you fit do to find whether friend correct? Explain why too.
z-m-03-08.s.s2.hint.0: Think how round column look from above too.
z-m-03-08.s.s2.hint.1: Find whether any viewing direction make ball and round column look different.
z-m-03-08.s.s2.selfAssess.0: With method wey I describe, fit you tell ball and round column apart?
z-m-03-08.s.s2.selfAssess.1: You talk say another object look same from above?
z-m-03-08.s.s2.selfAssess.2: You also think about the possibility say your friend fit be correct?
z-m-03-08.s.s2.model.0: You must look from side too. Round column also look circle from above, so e fit no be ball.
z-m-03-08.s.s2.model.1: You fit turn object and look from another side. Can shape also look circle from above, so no be sure say na ball.
z-m-03-08.s.s2.modelNote.1: You talk 'no sure' and give reason.
